Editor’s Note: The ETFs tracking benchmark indices, lede, economic data, and the headline were updated in the story.

U.S. stock futures were higher on Wednesday, as the Dow Jones, S&P 500, and Nasdaq 100 indices rose, following Tuesday’s lower close.

U.S. inflation topped Wall Street estimates in September, driven by higher energy costs. Headline CPI increased 0.6% month-over-month and 3.7% annually, surpassing forecasts of 0.5% and 3.6%, respectively. Meanwhile, core CPI—which excludes volatile food and energy prices—rose 0.3% on the month and 2.6% year-over-year, coming in slightly hotter than the projected 0.2% monthly rise and 2.4% annual pace.

Investors await the inflation data ahead of the opening bell. Morningstar reports that economists estimate the September Consumer Price Index (CPI) will increase by 0.5% month-over-month and 3.6% year-over-year, while core CPI is projected to rise 0.2% monthly and hold steady at 2.4% annually.

Boston Fed President Susan Collins said on Tuesday it would be “appropriate” to raise rates “a bit further” before year-end to return inflation to the Fed’s 2% target, while adding that her view will depend on incoming data. President Donald Trump said Taiwan has agreed to buy 30% of the liquefied natural gas from the proposed Alaska LNG project for the next 20 years, though Reuters reported the agreement’s detailed terms were not immediately clear and Taiwan’s government had not formally confirmed Trump’s figures.

Meanwhile, the 10-year Treasury bond yielded 5.20%, and the 2-year Treasury bond yielded 4.77% at the last check. The CME Group’s FedWatch tool projections show markets pricing in a 21.6% likelihood of the Federal Reserve hiking interest rates after its October meeting.

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY) and Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (NASDAQ:QQQ), which track the S&P 500 index and Nasdaq 100 index, respectively, were lower in premarket trading on Wednesday. The SPY was down 0.18% at $776.59, while the QQQ fell 0.46% to $740.16.

Cues From Last Session

U.S. stocks closed lower on Tuesday, with the Dow down over 100 points. Energy, communication services and utilities led, while health care, financials and industrials lagged.

Insights From Analysts

Professor Jeremy Siegel, senior economist to WisdomTree and emeritus professor of finance at The Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania, said rising real rates can signal stronger growth and he upgraded his equity view, writing that the economy still looks strong even as the market holds near all-time highs amid higher bond yields.

Siegel said he still expects the Fed to hold rates at its October meeting unless inflation data are “dramatically different from expectations,” while adding that he would not completely rule out another 25 or even 50 basis point increase later this year. He said bank deposits are still growing faster than what would be consistent with 2%–3% inflation and that the yield curve is steeper than its 40-year average, which he said are not signs of an economy that requires monetary easing.

On long-term equity returns, Siegel wrote that with the S&P 500 trading around 19 times earnings, the inverse P/E suggests roughly a 5.5% long-term real return, and he raised his estimate of long-term real equity returns to approximately 5.5%–6.5%. He said, “Higher rates are not necessarily bearish for stocks if those rates reflect stronger productivity and economic growth.”

Siegel said equities can continue to move higher if yields stabilize and growth expectations remain intact, and he flagged a risk he is monitoring: “The real danger would be a sudden technological breakthrough that makes a large portion of the current spending on data centers and compute obsolete.” He added, “But there is no evidence of that today.”

CoreWeave Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV), backed by Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA), is pursuing insurance-industry capital as AI infrastructure expansion increasingly depends on debt financing.

Brannin McBee, CoreWeave’s co-founder, told the Financial Times, in an interview published on Wednesday, that the company is seeking access to insurers’ large investment pools to secure potentially cheaper funding. McBee said stronger investment-grade credit ratings could help the company borrow from insurers, whose capital "is unlimited."

The company is also considering whether insurers could buy loans backed by lower-rated customers, including AI labs. McBee said those transactions are not yet prepared for the insurance market.

CoreWeave is evaluating additional delayed-draw term loans to speed data-center construction and equipment purchases. McBee compared the approach with financing power plants through contracts sold in advance.

He said future stock-market listings by AI labs could improve their credit profiles, while CoreWeave continues targeting a position among the industry’s largest infrastructure providers.

"If we stop building today, [we’d be] immensely cash-flow positive," he said. But "we are in a period where you have to be huge. You have to be one of the biggest players,” McBee said.

CoreWeave’s financing strategy arrives as executives across the technology and financial sectors warn that capital availability could become a major constraint on AI infrastructure growth.

Read Also: CoreWeave Unleashes Nvidia's Vera Rubin, Analyst Sees Room to Run

AI Boom Faces Funding Risks as Costs Rise

Co-founder McBee’s comments came as investor Chamath Palihapitiya questioned whether the AI boom is fueling a private-credit bubble after CoreWeave’s 2032 bond yield hit 15% before closing at a record 14.5%. He highlighted the growing reliance on debt, leases, and other financing, noting that U.S. direct lending surged from $96 billion in 2010 to $2.4 trillion in 2025. Technology firms accounted for $1.05 trillion, or 44%, of the 2025 direct-loan market, including more than $200 billion in loans to AI, big-data and cloud companies.

On Tuesday, Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon said AI computing demand continues to outpace supply but warned that heavy financing needs could raise borrowing costs and threaten some projects. He warned that rising interest rates may squeeze returns and make financing harder for some projects. However, he said demand for computing capacity continues to outpace supply, supporting further construction and financing activity.

Earlier this week, Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO) CEO Hock Tan warned that access to capital could become a bigger constraint on AI infrastructure expansion than chip or electricity shortages, with computing demand potentially exceeding supply through 2029 or 2030. Intel Corp. (NASDAQ:INTC) CEO Lip-Bu Tan flagged high borrowing costs and uncertainty over whether AI investments will deliver sufficient returns to justify the spending.

Price Action: Year-to-date, CoreWeave’s shares have surged 8.66%, as per Benzinga Pro. In Wednesday’s pre-market session, the stock is trading 6.70% lower at $72.60.

news.content:
The S&P 500 has gained approximately 14% in 2026, yet more than 40% of its constituent stocks have declined this year, according to Reuters.

The median S&P 500 stock has gained just 4%, while fewer than half of its constituents are trading above their 200-day moving averages, masking growing weakness beneath the surface.

As more index constituents struggle, the Magnificent Seven — a small group of U.S. mega-cap technology companies — remains the critical pillar of support, raising questions about how diversified investors really are when they own broad-market ETFs.

Read Also: S&P 500—What Happens In Q4 After A Negative September?

BTIG Warns Mag 7 Is The Market’s ‘Last Man Standing’

In a warning highlighted by ZeroHedge, BTIG chief market technician Jonathan Krinsky, in his technical note named “Last Man Standing,” cautioned that the Magnificent Seven’s continued strength has become a key support for the broader market.

That concentration extends directly into ETF portfolios. The Magnificent Seven accounted for approximately 34.8% of the S&P 500’s market capitalization as of Oct. 13, according to historical index-weight data.

That means investors in market-cap-weighted funds already have substantial exposure to Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA), Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL), Microsoft Corp (NASDAQ:MSFT), Amazon.com, Inc (NASDAQ:AMZN), Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL), Meta Platforms, Inc (NASDAQ:META) and Tesla, Inc (NASDAQ:TSLA), even without buying a dedicated technology or AI fund.

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY) provides broad exposure to the index, but its market-cap-weighting methodology gives the largest companies disproportionate influence over returns. The Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) offers another route into mega-cap growth stocks, potentially adding to concentration when held alongside an S&P 500 fund. Meanwhile, the Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF (BATS:MAGS) provides more direct exposure to the group.

Can Equal-Weight ETFs Offer an Alternative?

Investors seeking to reduce their dependence on mega-cap leaders could consider the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (NYSE:RSP). By assigning approximately equal weights to S&P 500 constituents at rebalancing, RSP spreads out the influence of the largest companies and increases exposure to smaller index members.

However, equal weighting is not automatically a safer bet. RSP can lag when mega-cap leaders continue outperforming and carries different sector-allocation and rebalancing risks.

Why Market Breadth Matters For ETF Investors

The bigger question is whether the S&P 500’s resilience reflects broad corporate strength or the performance of a handful of dominant companies. If the Magnificent Seven lose momentum before the rest of the market recovers, index funds could come under pressure despite their apparent diversification.

With market breadth weakening, investors may need to look beyond headline index returns to understand the concentration risk embedded in their ETF portfolios.

news.author: Daragh Thomas
news.content:
Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) is closing the gap with Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) in AI inference at a pace that has surprised even researchers who previously criticized AMD’s software.

SemiAnalysis researchers said Wednesday they watched AMD’s existing GPUs catch and briefly overtake some Nvidia configurations as engineers improved the software running on the chips over just weeks.

AMD’s Software Gains Surprise Researchers

“Lots of people have been anti-AMD for a long time, especially the AMD software ecosystem, including us,” SemiAnalysis host Jordan Nanos said during Wednesday’s podcast.

The firm’s InferenceX platform tracks how efficiently competing GPUs run GLM 5.3, a Chinese AI model used for complex tasks including coding.

Nvidia initially led, but AMD’s performance improved as engineers optimized its ATOM inference engine, which helps AI models generate responses. AMD eventually overtook some Nvidia configurations before the latter began recovering ground.

Researcher Wenyao Gao explained that while a chip’s hardware remains fixed after launch, engineers can continually improve the software controlling how efficiently it serves users.

In September research, SemiAnalysis found AMD’s MI355X delivered roughly 9% lower estimated inference costs than Nvidia’s B200 when both systems had to begin responding within two seconds.

Nvidia’s GB200 and GB300 systems remained cheaper in other configurations, however, highlighting how performance depends on the workload and response-time requirements.

Same Chips, Up to 38% More Performance

AMD’s improvements extend beyond the GLM 5.3 tests.

In September, AMD reported that its MI355X chips could handle up to 38% more AI work than in an earlier round of MLPerf, an industry benchmark that measures chip performance.

The striking part is that the hardware hadn’t changed. AMD achieved the improvement entirely through software updates.

In another comparison, a system using 72 AMD GPUs outperformed an earlier setup with 94 of the same chips. For cloud providers, that could mean serving more customers without buying additional hardware.

AMD is also finding ways to improve its software faster.

Futurum Research reported that AMD engineers are using AI agents to help write and optimize code. The company has also accelerated updates to its ROCm software platform, releasing new versions roughly every six weeks instead of every three months.

Nvidia’s CUDA software ecosystem still gives it a major advantage, but AMD is showing how quickly that gap can narrow without a new generation of chips.

Despite AMD’s progress, prediction traders continue to favor Nvidia’s broader market dominance. On Polymarket, Nvidia has approximately 76% odds of finishing 2026 as the world’s most valuable company, with $8.2 million traded.

Nvidia continues to benefit from intense GPU demand, but AMD’s improving software could give cloud providers a more competitive alternative without requiring a new generation of chips.

news.content:
On Tuesday, the script for the Federal Reserve’s October meeting looked settled. Policymakers would hold rates, wait for more data and let the midterm elections pass.

On Wednesday morning, a hotter-than-expected September consumer price index rewrote it.

Traders now see a 54% chance that the Fed raises rates at its Oct. 28 meeting.

A day earlier the chance was 20.7%, and a week ago it was 24.1%, according to 30-day fed funds futures tracked by CME FedWatch tool.

The economists reacting to the report are warning about more than one meeting.

They are talking about debasement. That is the relentless loss of the dollar’s purchasing power when a central bank lets inflation run.

The September CPI Report Beat Forecasts Where It Matters

The consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.6% in September after 0.4% in August, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said. That matched forecasts.

The annual rate climbed to 3.7% from 3.4%, above the 3.6% economists expected.

Gasoline did much of the work.

Pump prices rose 9.1% in the month and accounted for more than half of the overall increase. The energy index gained 5.2%.

However, the number that moved markets was core inflation.

Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, rose 0.3% in September against a 0.2% forecast.

The annual core rate rose to 2.6% from 2.4%, above the 2.5% consensus.

The gains were spread widely.

Recreation, used cars and trucks, education, airline fares, medical care and apparel all rose in the month, according to the BLS.

Why Economists Are Talking About Debasement

The debasement argument works in steps.

Prices rise faster than the Fed’s 2% target. If the central bank holds rates anyway, real interest rates (interest rates minus inflation) fall.

Savers then earn less, in real terms, for holding dollars. Some of that money moves into assets that cannot be printed, such as gold and other precious metals.

Robin Brooks, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, put it bluntly on X.

"Not a good CPI number," Brooks wrote. He noted that a spike in wireless services had driven last month’s core reading, which gave the Fed "a reasonable excuse" to pause.

"But today’s reading puts an October hike back on the table. If the Fed doesn’t hike, debasement wins."

In a second post, Brooks pointed to the political calendar. The odds of a hike would be higher, he wrote, if the October meeting were not "right before the midterms." The elections take place on Nov. 3.

"If the Fed doesn’t hike, it’ll be a big catalyst for gold and precious metals to take off," Brooks added.

Inflation Is No Longer Just an Energy Story

Jeffrey Roach, chief economist at LPL Financial, said the report shows price pressures moving beyond fuel.

"Inflation pressures are broadening beyond energy and are now filtering into other categories, including apparel and autos," Roach said.

He noted that new and used vehicle prices have now risen for three straight months, reversing the trend from earlier this year.

"As the Middle East conflict continues, inflation pressures are becoming more widespread across other categories," he added.

Nancy Vanden Houten, lead U.S. economist at Oxford Economics, pointed to an unusual source of pressure: technology.

Core prices rose with "widespread gains, including in sectors like computers and smartphones, as price pressures related to the AI building spillover to consumer goods," she said.

Oxford Economics expects a hike this month.

"The larger than expected increase in the core CPI in September increases the odds that the Federal Reserve raises rates at its meeting later this month, which is our forecast," Vanden Houten said.

Bond Traders Moved First

Treasury yields rose across the curve on Wednesday.

The two-year yield, the maturity most sensitive to Fed policy, climbed 10 basis points to 4.90%.

The 10-year yield rose about 7 basis points to 5.29%. That is still below the 5.34% it touched earlier this month, its highest level since 2002. The 30-year yield added 4 basis points to 5.60%.

The U.S. Dollar Index, which measures the dollar against six major currencies, gained 0.5% to 102.73.

Gold – as tracked by SPDR Gold Shares (NYSE:GLD) – fell 1.5% to about $4,100 an ounce, and silver dropped 3.7% to $56.95.

Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) slipped 0.2% to around $82,870.

The S&P 500 – tracked by the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY) – sunk 0.7%, minutes after the open in New York.

Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. (NYSE:BABA) is expanding its artificial intelligence push into consumer hardware, using new Qwen-powered wearables to make its Personal Agent technology a more active part of users’ daily lives.

Alibaba Launches New Qwen Glasses And Earbuds

Alibaba’s Qwen AI unit launched the Qwen Glasses N1 series and Qwen Clip earbuds, developed in collaboration with Bose.

The N1 glasses include a 50-megapixel camera and support continuous environmental awareness, translation, meeting summaries and voice services.

The N1 Pro adds real-time monitoring of heart rate, blood oxygen and skin temperature, along with eye tracking and iris identity verification, Yicai Global reported on Wednesday.

Alibaba also said the glasses support shopping, payments and health tracking. Users can interact with the AI agent through bone-conduction microphones.

The glasses offer up to 25 hours of standby time or nine hours of music playback per charge. The Qwen Clip earbuds support multilingual translation, live AI dictation and task assignment.

Meta Emerges As Key Smart-Glasses Rival

Alibaba is following a strategy similar to Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META), which has also positioned smart glasses as an entry point for AI assistants.

Bloomberg on Tuesday described Meta as the industry leader in the category. Meta recently expanded its lineup with a $349 camera-free model built primarily around its Muse AI assistant.

Alibaba’s new glasses start at 2,999 yuan, or about $450, before discounts, while the Pro version costs 3,499 yuan.

That pricing puts Alibaba in direct competition with Meta on features and quality rather than relying only on lower prices.

See More: Top Value Stocks

Qwen Targets A Broader Personal Agent Role

“The goal of Qwen is to become everyone’s Personal Agent,” Qwen Vice President Song Gang said. “We believe that AI wearables are an extension of Qwen in the physical world and an important part of Personal Agents.”

Alibaba wants the devices to move AI beyond simply responding to commands and toward helping users complete tasks more proactively.

An industry insider told Yicai that Alibaba is shifting competition away from standalone hardware specifications toward what AI agents can understand and execute.

By linking the glasses with Qwen models and Alibaba’s broader ecosystem, the company wants its AI to understand a user’s surroundings and access relevant services.

Alibaba Builds A Full-Stack AI Strategy

Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu has reiterated the company’s ambition to build across the full AI stack, spanning models, chatbot applications, AI chips, data centers and consumer hardware.

The company’s wearables therefore represent another layer of a broader strategy to connect AI infrastructure with end-user products and services.

Bitcoin and Leveraged Stock ETFs Lead the Pack

Alongside BITO, the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (NASDAQ:IBIT) averaged 45.8 million shares daily, placing it among the 10 most actively traded products.

However, their asset bases differ considerably. IBIT managed approximately $66.3 billion, compared with BITO’s $1.65 billion, highlighting how trading activity and fund size can tell different stories.

Leveraged single-stock ETFs also attracted substantial turnover. SNXX, which targets twice the daily performance of Sandisk Corp (NASDAQ:SNDK), averaged 83.3 million shares, while TSLL, which targets twice the daily performance of Tesla, Inc (NASDAQ:TSLA), recorded 80.6 million shares.

The GraniteShares 2x Short NVDA Daily ETF (NASDAQ:NVD) averaged 79 million shares despite managing just $58.5 million in assets. Its position highlights how a relatively small fund can generate significant trading activity when investors use it to express short-term views on Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA).

Semiconductor-Focused Products Occupy Several Top 10 Positions

The Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF (NYSE:SOXL) averaged 63.6 million shares daily, while its bearish counterpart, the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bear 3X ETF (NYSE:SOXS), recorded 62.5 million.

The Roundhill Memory ETF (BATS:DRAM), which provides exposure to memory-related stocks, averaged 47 million shares and reported $23.6 billion in AUM.

Meanwhile, the ProShares UltraPro QQQ (NASDAQ:TQQQ) averaged 53.8 million shares, compared with 48 million for the ProShares UltraPro Short QQQ (NASDAQ:SQQQ). Both funds offer leveraged exposure to the Nasdaq-100 in opposite directions.

TQQQ had approximately $39.5 billion in assets, versus $2.1 billion for SQQQ.

High Volume Does Not Mean Lower Risk

The rankings show that traders are gravitating toward products offering leveraged exposure to Bitcoin, individual stocks, semiconductors and the Nasdaq-100.

High average volume can indicate strong trading activity and help investors assess liquidity, but it does not guarantee tight bid-ask spreads or eliminate trading costs.

Moreover, leveraged ETFs generally target daily returns and can diverge significantly from their stated multiples over longer holding periods because of compounding and market volatility.

For investors, the takeaway is clear: the most actively traded ETFs can offer convenient vehicles for expressing market views, but popularity alone does not make them suitable long-term investments.

Contractor Pleads Guilty in Export Case

Ting-Wei "Willy" Sun, a contractor linked to Super Micro, pleaded guilty last Thursday in U.S. District Court in Manhattan, Reuters reported, citing a court filing. The case involves servers equipped with advanced chips from Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) in an alleged $2.5 billion scheme to export them to China.

Sun pleaded guilty to conspiring to violate U.S. export controls, smuggling, defrauding the U.S. government and obstructing justice.

Prosecutors allege that Sun and two others linked to Super Micro diverted AI servers to China starting in 2024. The indictment says the shipments violated U.S. export restrictions covering Nvidia’s B200, H100 and H200 chips.

Super Micro said it fired Sun and severed ties with the other defendants earlier this year.

Dell Technologies Inc. (NYSE:DELL) CEO Michael Dell warned that semiconductor shortages could worsen in 2027, suggesting memory supply constraints could persist for four years as AI demand outpaces manufacturing capacity.

“I do think it gets worse next year in terms of demand and supply,” Dell told CNBC’s David Faber on Tuesday.

When Faber asked specifically about memory, Dell added: “Maybe it’s a four-year problem because there’s just not enough supply.”

Why the Shortage Could Last Until 2030

Chipmakers are racing to catch up with demand they never saw coming. New factories take about four years to build, Dell said, meaning plants planned today may not begin production until 2029 or 2030.

But demand isn’t standing still. The first wave came from companies developing powerful AI models. Now Dell sees another emerging as businesses begin adopting the technology.

“Now we’re starting to see this wave in the enterprise. But it’s really just beginning,” Dell said.

ASML Holding NV (NASDAQ:ASML) said Wednesday its planned chipmaking-equipment supply would fall short of customer demand in 2027 and 2028. Some customers have expressed interest in placing orders for 2029 and 2030.

Semiconductor veteran Steve Williams told Benzinga last week that Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (NYSE:TSM) was effectively sold out of advanced manufacturing capacity for 2026, despite plans to spend up to $64 billion this year.

Williams identified advanced packaging, which combines AI processors with high-bandwidth memory, as another bottleneck.

Dell’s $95 Billion Backlog Meets Wall Street Doubts

Dell designs and deploys complete AI servers and data-center systems, combining Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) processors with memory, networking and cooling equipment.

The company reported $16.4 billion in quarterly AI server revenue and a record $95 billion backlog in September.

But scarce components can raise costs and delay deliveries, even as demand surges.

Barclays analyst Tim Long downgraded Dell from Overweight to Equal-Weight Wednesday, cutting his price target from $603 to $574. Dell shares fell around 8% in morning trading.

Long sees no meaningful acceleration yet in businesses purchasing their own AI infrastructure, contrasting with Dell’s confidence that enterprise adoption is just beginning.

The analyst still forecasts Dell’s AI server revenue tripling to $75 billion this fiscal year, but expects growth to slow over the following two years.

Despite those concerns, traders on Polymarket priced only a 6% chance of a qualifying AI industry downturn by December 31. The contract requires three severe events within 90 days, rather than merely slower investment.

Long estimates Dell’s AI server operating margins at around 5%, leaving the company with limited room to absorb higher component costs.

Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) is closing the gap with Anthropic in artificial intelligence, giving Guggenheim Securities fresh reason to back the stock. The next test is turning those gains into a business through its Muse AI agent.

Analyst Michael Morris maintained a Buy rating and raised his price target to $850 from $700 in an Oct. 14 note, citing higher 2027 estimates and the longer-term opportunity in agentic AI.

Meta now scores 56 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, behind only Anthropic’s 58 among the companies in the note’s comparison. Guggenheim sees the launch of Muse Wonder as a potential catalyst, provided the model’s capabilities translate into a more useful agent.

  • META stock is moving. See the chart and price action here.

The Big Question: How Does Muse Make Money?

Guggenheim expects Meta to follow a familiar playbook: let consumers use the product for free, then charge businesses to reach them.

"Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta’s core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," the analysts wrote.

The firm expects management to prioritize growing usage before near-term revenue. Muse reached 1.3 million daily active users after five weeks, up from 300,000 in its first week, according to Guggenheim’s analysis of Apptopia data.

Even so, that audience represents less than 0.05% of Meta’s 3.6 billion daily users. Guggenheim views free distribution across that enormous potential audience as an advantage as Meta competes to make AI agents part of everyday shopping, travel and scheduling.

A Costly Opportunity

Guggenheim raised its 2027 capital expenditure forecast to approximately $225 billion from $203 billion and expects free cash flow to remain under pressure through 2028.

A rival breakthrough could also force Meta into a prolonged spending race. Morris nevertheless pointed to the company’s record with WhatsApp globally and Reels against TikTok as reasons to believe it can emerge as a leader at scale.

Guggenheim expects agent monetization to ramp more significantly beyond 2027, supporting its willingness to assign Meta a higher valuation now. On the third-quarter earnings call, the firm will look for management to connect stronger models with a stronger agent business.

Without that connection, the analysts warned, the frontier model race becomes "a competitive cost center rather than a growth investment."

Dell Technologies Inc. (NYSE:DELL) stock fell more than 11% on Wednesday after a Barclays downgrade, even as CEO Michael Dell highlighted strong demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure and growing enterprise adoption.

Barclays analyst Tim Long downgraded the stock from Overweight to Equal-Weight and lowered his price forecast to $574 from $603.

Long cited Dell’s stretched valuation and said broader enterprise technology spending has yet to see a significant boost from AI adoption.

Despite Wednesday’s selloff, Dell shares have gained more than 300% in 2026, supported by strong AI server orders and a growing enterprise backlog.

However, Michael Dell struck an optimistic tone in a Wednesday CNBC interview, suggesting that the AI infrastructure boom still has years of growth ahead.

Dell Sees AI Demand Outpacing Supply Through 2030

Dell told CNBC that demand for AI infrastructure continues to exceed supply, a trend he expects to persist through 2030.

He acknowledged that long-term forecasts remain uncertain. However, he pointed to the time required to expand semiconductor manufacturing capacity.

A new chip fabrication plant can take about four years to build, while AI models and their capabilities are advancing much faster.

Meanwhile, increasingly powerful AI systems require newer semiconductors, more memory and greater computing capacity. These requirements are pushing up system costs while driving further infrastructure investment.

See More: Top Value Stocks

Enterprise AI Adoption Is Just Beginning

Dell said frontier AI labs and major technology companies led the initial wave of AI infrastructure spending. Now, broader enterprise adoption is beginning to emerge as another growth driver.

He said AI’s economic impact is already becoming visible, describing the technology’s potential as significant.

However, he emphasized that enterprise adoption remains in its early stages, suggesting companies will need to invest heavily in computing infrastructure as AI use expands.

Dell Explains Its Role Alongside NVIDIA

Dell also distinguished his company’s role from that of NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) and CEO Jensen Huang.

He explained that NVIDIA helps develop the technology behind advanced AI systems, while Dell focuses on building the infrastructure customers need to deploy and operate them.

That distinction also shapes Dell’s approach to AI safety. Rather than controlling how individual models are used, the company concentrates on supplying the underlying computing systems.

Still, Dell acknowledged the need for safeguards as AI capabilities advance. He said governments and businesses must establish appropriate guidelines while allowing technological progress to continue.

He expressed confidence about AI’s future through 2030 but stressed that the industry must continue addressing potential risks.

ASML Holding N.V. (NASDAQ:ASML) has secured higher prices for its most critical chipmaking equipment as the artificial intelligence boom strengthens its bargaining power with semiconductor manufacturers.

The Dutch company confirmed Wednesday that negotiations with customers have concluded, with the increases expected to boost revenue and profit margins starting in 2027.

“We thought that we were entitled to a higher percentage,” CFO Roger Dassen said during the company’s third-quarter earnings call.

“There was a clear acceptance that maybe the overall value in the ecosystem is shifting,” CEO Christophe Fouquet said, linking the change partly to AI.

Fouquet said it was one of the first times in many years ASML had held such pricing discussions with customers.

AI Boom Strengthens ASML’s Hand

ASML is the only commercial supplier of extreme ultraviolet lithography machines, which chipmakers need to manufacture the most advanced semiconductors.

In July, The Information reported that Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (NYSE:TSM), ASML’s largest customer, was resisting proposed increases.

ASML has now completed negotiations, although it hasn’t identified which customers agreed to higher prices or disclosed the size of the increases.

Its bargaining position has strengthened as manufacturers race to expand production.

ASML said its planned output for 2027 and 2028 won’t fully meet customer demand, even as it expands capacity. Some customers are already seeking equipment for 2029 and 2030.

Beyond today’s equipment shortages, ASML’s next growth cycle may depend on when chipmakers adopt its more advanced High-NA EUV machines at scale, with Samsung targeting 2028 and TSMC 2030.

Higher Prices to Boost Margins From 2027

The increases cover ASML’s most critical manufacturing equipment, with prices for productivity upgrades to existing machines expected to follow.

They should begin lifting revenue and margins in 2027, with the full impact arriving in 2028.

Asked by JPMorgan analyst Sandeep Deshpande how much of the increase would become profit, Dassen said some would cover manufacturing expansion costs, but a significant portion would boost gross margins.

ASML reported a 57.5% gross margin in the third quarter but expects around 57% in the fourth quarter, mainly because of production expansion costs. The new price increases have yet to take effect.

Asked by Berenberg analyst Tammy Qiu whether ASML could repeat the increases annually, management said that wasn’t the plan.

“We don’t want to be in a position that as the market goes down that we’re actually having discussions with customers on price decreases,” Dassen said.

AI Stocks Slide Despite Strong Demand

The upbeat outlook contrasted with Wednesday morning’s sharp selloff in AI stocks.

Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) fell 5%, Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) lost 3% and TSMC dropped 3%. CoreWeave Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV) plunged about 11%.

D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria warned CoreWeave shareholders could lose everything if AI spending weakens, citing expensive borrowing and insufficient investment returns.

On Polymarket, traders assigned a 6% chance of a qualifying AI-industry downturn by December 31, rising to 19% by June 2027.

ASML’s U.S.-listed shares fell 1% Wednesday despite its stronger pricing outlook.

BlackRock Inc. (NYSE:BLK) expects momentum to continue into the seasonally strong fourth quarter, supported by broad activity across iShares, private markets, retirement and international platforms, the company said during its third-quarter earnings call.

Management said the company continues to execute against its long-term targets for organic base fee growth, operating margin expansion and EPS.

BlackRock repurchased $550 million of shares in the third quarter of 2026 and expects to buy back at least another $550 million in the fourth quarter, subject to market conditions and capital spending plans, consistent with guidance issued in July.

• BlackRock stock is trading in a tight range. What should traders watch with BLK?

Growth Opportunities In AI and Private Markets

The company sees growth opportunities in the convergence of public and private markets, rising AI infrastructure investment, and increasing demand for investment technology and data.

Management also expects private credit demand to remain strong, particularly from insurers seeking high-grade investment solutions, with activity potentially accelerating toward year-end and into 2027.

BlackRock raised $68 billion in private markets over the past 12 months, including $25 billion in private credit during its first full year with HPS.

Its AI infrastructure partnership completed its first deployment with the closing of the Align Data Center transaction, valued at approximately $40 billion in enterprise value.

The company also partnered with Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) to finance its planned $14 billion Texas data center, combining Global Infrastructure Partners’ infrastructure expertise with private financing capabilities, including HPS.

BlackRock sees further opportunities to fund customers expanding computing capacity, initially through private placements for high-grade insurance mandates and potentially later through securitized, tradable investments available to a wider range of investors.

Management said BlackRock will use its technology, data, scale and investment expertise to develop standardized performance measures and risk analytics for computing capacity as an emerging asset class.

Earnings Snapshot

BlackRock reported third-quarter revenue growth of 19% year-over-year to $7.75 billion, topping the analyst consensus estimate of $7.52 billion. Adjusted earnings came in at $15.93 per share, ahead of the consensus estimate of $14.13.

J.P. Morgan analyst Michael Cho said revenue topped JPMorgan’s $7.47 billion estimate, partly due to higher performance fees.

Cho noted that BlackRock’s third-quarter results exceeded expectations, supported by strong inflows across most businesses.
